subject: Social Science

slides.title: Timeline and Sources of History
bullets: Class 6 — CBSE Social Science
Chapter 4
slides.speaker_notes: How we organise time, and how we know what we know about the past.

slides.title: What you'll be able to do
bullets: Define a timeline and what it shows.
Use BCE / CE and remember 'no year zero'.
Sort events into Ancient / Medieval / Modern.
Tell archaeological, literary and oral sources apart.
Explain stratigraphy and radiocarbon dating.

slides.title: What a timeline shows
bullets: Earlier events on the LEFT, later on the RIGHT.
Spacing reflects elapsed years.
It shows ORDER.
It shows DURATION (length of an event).
It shows SIMULTANEITY (what was happening elsewhere).

slides.title: Counting years — BCE and CE
bullets: 1 CE is the reference point.
Years before = BCE; years after = CE.
Bigger BCE = EARLIER (3000 BCE older than 2000 BCE).
Bigger CE = LATER (2000 CE later than 1000 CE).
NO YEAR ZERO — 1 BCE → 1 CE directly.

slides.title: How many years between two dates?
bullets: Both BCE: subtract. (3000 BCE → 1500 BCE = 1500 years.)
Both CE: subtract. (500 CE → 1500 CE = 1000 years.)
Across the divide: ADD and subtract 1. (100 BCE → 100 CE = 199 years.)
Why subtract 1? No year zero!

slides.title: Big blocks of time
bullets: Decade = 10 years.
Century = 100 years (21st century = 2001–2100).
Millennium = 1000 years.
Stone, Bronze, Iron Age = main material for tools.
Indian eras: Vikram Samvat (57 BCE), Shaka Samvat (78 CE).

slides.title: Three broad periods of Indian history
bullets: ANCIENT — up to ~700 CE: Harappan, Vedic, Mauryan, Gupta.
MEDIEVAL — ~700 CE to ~1700 CE: Cholas, Delhi Sultanate, Vijayanagara, Mughals.
MODERN — ~1700 CE onwards: British rule, freedom struggle, Independence.
These are convenient labels, not sharp walls.
Change is gradual.

slides.title: How we know the past — sources
bullets: A SOURCE is any surviving evidence about the past.
Three families: archaeological, literary, oral.
ARCHAEOLOGICAL — physical objects: pottery, coins, ruins, bones, seeds.
LITERARY — written texts: Vedas, epics, Tripiṭakas, inscriptions.
ORAL — songs, stories, family genealogies.

slides.title: Sort these into the right family
bullets: A coin → archaeological.
The Rigveda → literary.
Grandmother's family song → oral.
An Ashoka edict → literary (carved inscription).
A piece of charcoal → archaeological.

slides.title: Archaeology — digging up the past
bullets: Archaeologists EXCAVATE sites layer by layer.
STRATIGRAPHY — older lies DEEPER.
If Pot A is below Pot B, A is older.
Famous Indian sites: Mohenjo-daro, Harappa, Dholavira, Lothal, Sānchī, Hampi, Ajanta, Ellora.
Each layer tells a part of the story.

slides.title: Putting numbers on dates — radiocarbon
bullets: RADIOCARBON (C-14) DATING measures C-14 in once-living material.
Wood, charcoal, bone, seeds — all once alive.
The older the sample, the less C-14 left.
Cannot date pure stone or pure metal.
Gives an age in years (with a small uncertainty).

slides.title: Texts that tell us the past
bullets: The four VEDAS — Ṛig, Sāma, Yajur, Atharva.
The two epics — Mahābhārata and Rāmāyaṇa.
Buddhist Tripiṭakas (Pāli); Jaina Āgamas (Prakrit).
Sangam literature in TAMIL — South India.
Inscriptions — carved on stone / copper / pillars.

slides.title: Ashoka's edicts and old coins
bullets: Ashoka carved inscriptions on rocks and pillars (3rd c. BCE).
They tell us about his policies and his moral law (dhamma).
Coins show kings' names, languages and symbols.
A coin found far from where it was minted = trade.
A king's inscription rarely tells us his FAILURES.

slides.title: Asking questions of a source
bullets: WHO made it?
WHEN was it made?
WHY was it made?
WHAT does it leave OUT?
Does ANOTHER source agree?

slides.title: You try (5 minutes)
bullets: 1. How many years between 2000 BCE and 1000 CE?
2. Sort: Mauryas, Cholas, Mughals, Independence — into Ancient / Medieval / Modern.
3. Name one source for each family.
4. Why can a stone tool not be C-14 dated?
5. List three things you'd ask of a king's inscription.

slides.title: Quick check
bullets: Q1. Bigger BCE number — earlier or later?
Q2. Decade vs century vs millennium — which is biggest?
Q3. The Vedas — archaeological or literary source?
Q4. Stratigraphy: older lies — deeper or higher?
Show fingers.

slides.title: Key takeaways
bullets: Timeline = order + duration + simultaneity.
BCE/CE: bigger BCE = older; bigger CE = later; NO year zero.
Decade 10 / century 100 / millennium 1000 years.
Indian history: Ancient → Medieval → Modern (~700 CE, ~1700 CE).
Three source families: archaeological, literary, oral.
Stratigraphy = relative dates; radiocarbon = absolute dates.
Always cross-check sources and ask WHO / WHEN / WHY / WHAT IS LEFT OUT.
